correctness.rationale: For the displayed map and σ₁σ₂η ≠ 0, let H(y)=ηy|y|/2−y and Q=z−σ₂H(y). On a transition with both endpoints in a single closed half-line, H restricts to one quadratic and ΔQ is ∓σ₂η x²/2, including zero endpoints. Thus a one-sided string of N transitions wholly in the box has Σx² ≤ 4B_R/|σ₂η|. The derivative bound for the sigmoid gives |x_{j+1}−σ₁/2| ≤ L_R|x_j|, hence x_j²+x_{j+1}² ≥ σ₁²/[4(1+L_R²)]. Summing N−1 adjacent pairs gives N≤1+C_R; a floor(C_R)+3 time block has floor(C_R)+2 transitions, strictly more than this. This excludes each closed half-line and thus forces both strict signs. Continuity gives forward invariance of the support of a stationary law (preimages of neighborhoods of an image point have positive mass), and integration of the block indicator inequalities gives the two 1/M_R bounds. At σ₃=0, the x-iterates from time 1 have the sign of σ₁ and magnitude at most |σ₁|, and from time 2 magnitude at least δ. Summation gives the stated y bound; thereafter the z increments have eventual sign sgn(σ₂σ₁η) and magnitude bounded below by a positive linear function of time, yielding quadratic escape. Eq. (9) has θ=s−1+Υ, so at Υ=1 the current-state −x₁ cancels exactly in the first forward-difference step.
residual_risks: No claim about genuinely fractional orders, the existence of bounded orbits, or the optimal return constant. Finite trajectory diagnostics were not used to establish recurrence.

value.rationale: The exact signed coboundary links the absence of one-sided recurrence to a uniform quantitative constraint on any compact invariant law of the named model. This supplies an analytic diagnostic beyond numerical chaos evidence and absence of equilibria. The zero-feedback estimates identify a necessary coupling condition for boundedness and distinguish drift of the two memory coordinates.
residual_risks: The constants may be conservative, and the result gives no guarantee that a compact recurrent set exists for any nonzero feedback.
